archetype.name: Dual-Threat (efficiency-first passer)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose legs still move the chains, but who in 2026 did his real damage as a precise, aggressive passer on modest volume, with the run game as a supplement rather than the engine.

report.headline: Best per-dropback passer in football for four games, now waiting on a thumb.
report.take:
For four weeks Lamar Jackson was the most efficient passer in the league on a per-play basis. His 10.63 adjusted net yards per dropback ranked first among 47 qualifiers, his 9.97 yards per attempt second, and his +8.29 CPOE third. It did not show up as volume. He threw only 19.4 times a game in an offense that passes less than situation predicts (-2.5 pass rate over expected), so his 193.4 passing yards a game ranked 26th. This was a quarterback being asked to do less and doing it about as well as anyone can.

The engine was accuracy beyond the sticks. On throws of 10+ air yards he averaged 0.776 EPA, with the intermediate band at 0.812 and the deep band at 0.745, and Zay Flowers turned 20 targets into 1.359 EPA apiece. Underneath he was efficient too: 79.6% completions and five of his six touchdowns came on 0-9 yard throws. The rushing is quieter than his prime, at 3.8 carries a game, but it is still sharp: scrambles averaged 0.48 EPA and moved the chains on six of ten. The game-by-game path climbed. His CPOE rose every week from 4.8 to 11.3 through Week 4, and his pass EPA topped 11 in each of Weeks 3 and 4.

The numbers flatter him in a few places. A +8.29 CPOE sits far above anything in his career; his best previous season was 4.55 in 2024. His bad-throw rate (16.5%, 32nd of 38) is in line with what he has always charted, so the completion surge leans on throw selection and receivers as much as on newfound ball placement. The situational splits are also ordinary: third down was flat at 0.01 EPA with a 34.8% conversion rate, and the red zone was slightly negative even with four touchdowns.

Availability is the bigger issue. He left Week 4 after 52% of snaps, missed three Huntley starts, returned against Buffalo and lasted 2% of snaps. He is now headed for right-thumb surgery and injured reserve, with an estimated return around December 13. When he comes back, expect the efficiency to settle toward his career norms. The decisive unknown is how a surgically repaired throwing-hand thumb affects the accuracy that drove this season.

strengths.title: League-best efficiency per dropback
strengths.body: He led qualifiers in adjusted net yards per dropback and ranked fourth in EPA per dropback. He did it by completing passes at a high rate without sacrificing depth, and by keeping interceptions rare (1% of attempts). The efficiency is real, but it rests on 97 attempts and a CPOE well beyond his career peak, so some of it is a hot sample.

strengths.title: Punishing defenses past ten yards
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards produced more EPA per play than his short game, which is unusual for anyone. Flowers was the main beneficiary, at more than a point of EPA per target. Deep completion rate (44.4%) is normal for a vertical thrower, so this reflects aggression paying off rather than freak precision, and it is the most transferable part of his game.

strengths.title: Scrambles as a drive extender
strengths.body: Rushing volume is down from his prime, but when plays broke down his scrambles averaged 0.48 EPA and converted six first downs on ten tries. That helps explain why his long time to throw (3.11 seconds) did not inflate his sack rate. His 29.2% pressure-to-sack rate is a big improvement on last year's figure.

concerns.title: Throwing-hand thumb surgery
concerns.body: He has not finished a game since Week 3: he left Week 4 at 52% of snaps and Week 8 at 2%. He is now going on IR after surgery on his right thumb, with an estimated return of December 13, which is a target, not a promise. A repaired thumb on the throwing hand is exactly the kind of injury that can dull accuracy and grip on the throws that powered this season.

concerns.title: Completion surge outruns his history
concerns.body: His CPOE is up 6.5 points on last season and well past his 2024 career best. Meanwhile his bad-throw rate actually ticked up and ranks near the bottom. The gap points to favorable throw selection and receiver play inflating the completion numbers, so some regression is likely even with a healthy thumb.

concerns.title: Ordinary on money downs
concerns.body: For all the per-play brilliance, third down was break-even and the red zone slightly negative. Both came on small samples (23 and 15 plays), with long average distances on third down (9.2 to go). This is more noise and situation than a flaw, but it is why the touchdown output looked merely good.

trend.note: His play climbed through September, with CPOE rising every week and pass EPA above 11 in Weeks 3 and 4. Injury then cut Week 4 short, cost him three games, and ended his Week 8 return after one throw.

nextGame.headline: He's out; Baltimore digs deep into its quarterback room.
nextGame.body:
Jackson will not play Thursday against Jacksonville; he is headed to IR after thumb surgery. That is a shame on paper, because this is a defense he could have attacked. The Jaguars rank third in overall defensive EPA, first against short passes and second against the run, yet 29th against deep throws, and his 10+ air-yard game was the best part of his season. Their back end is also thinning: safety Antonio Johnson is out and safety Eric Murray is done for the year.

The availability around him is grim for Baltimore. Tyler Huntley, who started Weeks 5-7, "probably" won't play on his sprained toe, and Joe Fagnano was limited with an ankle injury. Up front, guard Olaivavega Ioane is out and every-snap starters Roger Rosengarten and John Simpson are questionable on a four-day turnaround. The Book makes the Ravens 8.5-point home underdogs at +340, which tells you how much of this team's ceiling left with him.

keyMatchups.title: Who takes the snaps
keyMatchups.body: With Jackson out and Huntley trending toward missing the game, Baltimore may start a quarterback who has barely played. That matters more than any scheme detail and is the main reason the line sits where it does.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area defense vs. deep leaks
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville smothers short throws and leaks deep EPA. That profile rewards a quarterback who can push the ball accurately downfield, which is exactly what Jackson did this year and what a backup may not be trusted to do.

keyMatchups.title: Run game into a wall
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore's fallback would be the run. Jacksonville ranks second against it and first in EPA allowed to lead backs, while a banged-up interior line is missing Ioane.

nextGame.watch: Any update on the surgery timeline and whether Baltimore's December 13 target holds.

restOfSeason.body:
The question is not how good he is but how many games remain and how his hand responds. If he returns around mid-December, he likely gets the final stretch of the regular season. Expect the volume to stay modest in a run-leaning offense, at roughly 185-235 passing yards a game. Expect his efficiency to drift down from league-best toward the top-ten range his career suggests, because the CPOE spike and the deep-ball EPA on 18 attempts are the parts most likely to cool.

The rushing should hold at its current, reduced level, and the scramble value is a durable trait. The first game or two back from throwing-thumb surgery deserve caution, both for accuracy and for how freely the staff lets him run. Fantasy value in those games rests on efficiency rather than volume, so a 15-20 PPR range is a fair expectation if healthy.
swingFactors: Whether the December 13 return target holds
Grip and accuracy after thumb surgery
Health of the Ravens' interior line

confidence.note: Out with thumb surgery; 97-attempt sample with an outlier CPOE.
